correctness.rationale: The derivation follows by conditioning on the uniformly selected update vertex: centered single-edge bits are eigenfunctions of K with eigenvalue r, so each product over edge subset S is an eigenfunction with lambda_S=1-omega+omega/N sum_v r^{d_S(v)}; product Bernoulli(pi) is the unique stationary law. Differences for adjacent versus disjoint pairs and triangle versus claw triples equal omega(1-r)^2/N and omega(1-r)^3/N, strictly positive for all admissible rates. Whitney line-graph inversion then reconstructs labelled incidence. The seven-vertex claw/triangle-swap witness has exactly equal one-/two-edge projected Markov chains; a standard-library exact rational 64-state checker verified full stationary laws, 126 nontrivial eigenfunction relations, all first/second-order signatures and 9/224 triple gap. All quantifiers and the edge-labelled nature of the lower bound are explicit.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete and sharp identifiability classification for a specific social-interaction stochastic environment: determine full pairwise network incidence from an observable moment hierarchy. It explains why pairwise edge trajectory data universally identify adjacent pairs but cannot distinguish which component is a three-star and which is a triangle in a disconnected graph, and identifies a minimal additional three-edge measurement that resolves the ambiguity. The two-order lower bound matches all parameters and vertex count, providing substantive information-theoretic content beyond a worked example; finite-sample robustness is not claimed.
